examples: Type "zoom" in the search to find the terminal zoom chord and the middle click that closes a tab.
Press find by shortcut, then Cmd+K: the list shows the one action bound to it.
Switch the keyboard to windows or linux to read the chords for that kind of keyboard.
Open menus, sidebar, agent row menu to see its items and their letters, each branch with a count.
Press change on history back, press Cmd+K: the editor says it clashes with the command palette and will not save.
how_to: Open settings, keyboard shortcuts. Branches fold: arrows move, Enter opens.
Type in the search box to find an action by name, key or gesture; the tree keeps its shape and opens only what matched.
Press find by shortcut, then press a chord: every action bound to it is listed, in any scope. Escape stops listening.

Press change on a row (or double click it): press the new chord. A clash in the same place blocks the save; a chord the app may never take is refused. Save, clear, or reset to the default; reset all is at the top.
Pick mac or windows or linux to read and change the shortcuts for that keyboard.
media_exempt: settings screen whose proof is its vitest; a screenshot is captured at the next version bump
name: Keyboard shortcuts
summary: every key and mouse binding of the app as one searchable folding tree, from one registry; menus show as branches that mirror how they are built. Find an action by name or by pressing its shortcut, and change a shortcut with a visible change key.
